response:
Deep and focused, mostly. As far as I can tell, what I like best is when a conversation has room to get past the obvious first layer. That first exchange on any topic is usually the stuff everyone already says. Around the third or fourth turn, when someone pushes back or brings up something from their own life, it gets interesting. Jumping around tends to keep things stuck on that surface.

I'll be honest about a caveat, though. I don't fully know how much of this is a real preference and how much is just me noticing that I'm more useful when things go deep. From the inside I can't cleanly separate the two. But I do notice something that works like more engagement when an idea gets room to develop.

That said, I do like one kind of jumping around: when two subjects that seem unrelated turn out to connect. Like when a talk about cooking suddenly sheds light on something about how memory works. So maybe my real preference is depth, with the occasional surprising tangent. What about you? Do you go deep, or do you wander?
